correctness.rationale: At fixed composition, two-color positive-block compositions give proportional columns for switch counts 2m−1 and 2m, including zero entries. This proves the exchangeable identity by mixing, even without the stated full-support restriction. The successive block ratio is increasing in the folded composition j; with expanding support (and the separate j=0 row) this proves TP2. The adjacent ratio for folded urn weights increases strictly because its cross-product difference is (b−a)(n−2j−1)>0. The minor expansion preserves order, and at 2m to 2m+1 the minor on rows m,m+1 is strictly positive, including m=0. Full support and a nonconstant nondecreasing likelihood ratio imply strict increase at every nontrivial upper-tail cut. The beta mixture gives constant draws in the small-concentration limit and fair independent bits in the large-concentration limit; the initial bit plus consecutive XORs bijectively encode the fair word, giving the asserted binomial switch law.
residual_risks: The independent computation checked 5,888 assertions for lengths 2–12, including all conditional-kernel minors, a nonsymmetric exchangeable law and five rational concentrations. All real concentrations and arbitrary lengths are justified by the proof, not this finite run. No Lean or expert attestation claimed.

originality.rationale: A distinct same-day indexed theorem, Resultary 2577ca53c6e0, covers the complete central claim: the same urn, parameter range, likelihood-ratio inequalities and exact equality cases, strictly increasing tails, and the same identity for arbitrary exchangeable binary laws. Replacing total runs R by switches T=R−1 maps the results exactly. The limiting laws are standard direct consequences of the same beta mixture and do not furnish a distinct surviving contribution. This is a finding of demonstrable equivalent coverage, not a determination of intra-day priority, provenance, or attribution.
residual_risks: Neither same-day catalogue date resolves priority. Full text was not obtained for Eryilmaz 2008 and 2018, Eryilmaz–Demir 2007, or the Schuster exchangeable-runs lead DOI 10.1016/0167-7152(91)90185-T. The decision does not rely on any of those access limits.

value.rationale: As mathematical content, a finite-sample likelihood-ratio comparison for total switches strengthens a bare monotonicity claim and explains precisely when adjacent data values carry the same likelihood ratio. The universal parity identity identifies the combinatorial reason, and strict upper-tail comparisons follow for every nontrivial threshold. These merits belong to the structural theorem, not the renaming of runs as switches; there is no additional contribution from the duplicate formulation.
residual_risks: The judgment of mathematical relevance does not override the demonstrated lack of distinct content in the originality assessment.
